# LINT-150 native oscillator output path fixtures

These tooling-owned synthetic schematics exercise native KiCad netlist export
for `oscillator.output_load_path_mismatch`. The authored requirement maps X1.1
through fitted R1 to U2.2 and U3.3, with an inclusive nominal resistance range
of 22–47 ohms. The boundary control uses 47R. The fault keeps the same topology
but uses 1k, which must produce a review with the parsed nominal value.

| Fixture                             | SHA-256                                                            | Expected result                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `series-boundary-control.kicad_sch` | `4fadcabb12a2bbedc396e707abf0bf1247df3a921674b5236cc993c9d54445b9` | No mapped-path finding at the inclusive upper boundary.    |
| `wrong-value-fault.kicad_sch`       | `9225ef72ca1e7922003672085bc69531a33f67b0acc1acbde2b9554d350239d8` | REVIEW reports R1 at 1000 ohms against the authored range. |

The sources are generated by
[`oscillator_output_path_native.py`](../../../design_lint_fixtures/oscillator_output_path_native.py)
and validated by the lint-marked source-integrity regression. The exact native
lane repeats exports and evaluates the typed netlist from digest-pinned KiCad
10.0.0 and 10.0.5 images. The project contract and fixtures are synthetic;
they do not assert that real oscillator outputs need a series resistor.

Run the focused native acceptance lane with:

```sh
KICAD_RUN_NATIVE_OSCILLATOR_OUTPUT_PATH_FIXTURES=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -I -m pytest -q \
  tests/test_oscillator_output_paths_native_fixture_lane.py \
  -m 'design_lint and component_lint and native_kicad'
```
